opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but admin is only for the owning role (Engineer). As a full-time employee, max is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Traci Lowe (E041) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; never admin). Requested admin on Source Code, so grant max read.
reason: Traci Lowe (E041) requested admin on Source Code. Admin is only permitted for the owning role (Engineer), and Traci's role is Analyst, so admin is off the table regardless. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR says full-time (max write) while Security DB says contractor with basic training (max read; write requires advanced training). Because the records conflict, I grant the highest level that is compliant under both readings. Read satisfies policy in either case (full-time max write ≥ read; contractor with basic training max read). Granting read.
